Inconspicuous

in-kun-SPIK-yoo-us -- Latin in- ('not') + conspicuous (con- 'together' + specere 'to look'). · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Inconspicuous is not easily noticed; blending in rather than standing out.

The undercover officer chose an inconspicuous gray sedan instead of anything that might draw attention.

Worked Example

Hoping nobody would notice she'd arrived twenty minutes late, she slipped into the back row and tried to stay inconspicuous for the rest of the assembly.

That effort to blend in and avoid drawing any attention at all is exactly what it means to be inconspicuous.

How Inconspicuous Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

unnoticeable

unnoticeable: hard to notice, though not necessarily on purpose

camouflaged

camouflaged: deliberately disguised to blend completely into the surroundings

Antonyms

prominent

prominent: very noticeable or standing out clearly

flashy

flashy: showy and deliberately attention-grabbing

How Strong Is It? — unnoticeable → camouflaged → inconspicuous

unnoticeable vs. inconspicuous

unnoticeable vs. inconspicuous: The small crack in the sidewalk was so unnoticeable that most people walked right over it.

camouflaged vs. inconspicuous

camouflaged vs. inconspicuous: The moth's wings were so perfectly camouflaged against the bark that the bird flew right past it.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — in-

prefix — in-: not (Latin)

root — -spic-

root — -spic-: to look, see (Latin (specere))

suffix — -uous

suffix — -uous: full of, tending to (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Inconspicuous combines in- ('not') with the root -spic- ('to look, see') and -uous ('full of, tending to') -- so something inconspicuous is, quite literally, not apt to be looked at, easily passed over by the eye.

Root Check

Word Choice

Inconspicuous usually describes something that simply doesn't draw the eye, whether by accident or on purpose -- it's a slightly more formal word than 'plain' or 'unnoticeable.'
